hints.title: Exhaustive Window Search Obstacle
hints.text: Testing every substring of s to check if it contains all characters of t takes O(|s|^2 * |t|) time. How can you expand a range until all required characters are present, then contract it from the left to find the minimal valid span?

hints.title: Frequency Deficit and Contraction Invariant
hints.text: Track required character counts from t. Expand the right boundary to satisfy all character needs, then shrink the left boundary while all counts remain satisfied to minimize the window.

hints.title: Formed Counter and Dynamic Two Pointers
hints.text: Count character frequencies in t and track how many distinct characters have met their target. Advance right, incrementing window counts. When all distinct required characters are satisfied, advance left to shrink the window while recording the minimum valid length, until a requirement is violated.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Each character in s is visited at most twice (once by right pointer, once by left pointer).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all O(|S|^2) substrings by checking character counts against t takes O(|S|^2 * |T|) time, leading to time limit exceeded.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing character frequencies in two hash tables uses O(|S| + |T|) space to enable linear O(|S| + |T|) window expansion and contraction.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using a "formed" variable to track satisfied distinct character counts (avoiding comparing the entire map on every step), correct left-shrinking loop, and returning empty string when no valid window exists.
